tasks.title: P2.1 env-readiness-FSM health_probe PRODUCER Implementation
acceptance_criteria: Create ngv2/health_producer.py which defines produce_health_input.
Standard library only at module top, no new subpackage, no module-level side effects.
Quarantine import side effects behind import_fn seam, default does target import.
Quarantine service-start side effects behind start_fn seam, default starts service subprocess.
Quarantine loopback bind health-poll side effects behind probe_fn seam, default does socket connect/poll.
For library targets, do not require bind or start.
For service targets, run start_fn and probe_fn; set service_bound, health_route_ok, bound_addr, and start_cmd.
Exceptions in seams are caught and fail-closed.
Returns the exact dict shape required by fsm_health_probe.health_probe.

functional_requirements: Define produce_health_input(jail_artifact, provision_artifact, *, import_fn=..., start_fn=..., probe_fn=...) -> dict in ngv2/health_producer.py.
Standard library only imports at module top level, no module-level side effects.
Fail closed with import_ok=False and return immediately if import_fn fails or raises.
Identify library targets and return import_ok=True, is_service=False without invoking service logic.
For service targets, call start_fn and probe_fn to start and verify bind.
Fail closed on service start or probe failures/exceptions.
Return the exact keys required by fsm_health_probe.health_probe for both paths.
spec.interfaces: Function signature: produce_health_input(jail_artifact: dict, provision_artifact: dict | None, *, import_fn: Callable = ..., start_fn: Callable = ..., probe_fn: Callable = ...) -> dict
edge_cases: import_fn raises ImportError or returns False.
Target is classified as a service but fails to bind loopback.
non_goals: Integration of the health_producer into run_hunt or the conductor is out of scope.
Mutating live FSM phases or lists is out of scope.
spec.implementation_notes:
No third-party packages allowed. Implement real defaults using standard library socket and subprocess/thread modules. For credentials/secrets, avoid hardcoding strings. Use deterministic helper parameters if clock or randomness is needed.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.
